project.name: Sample Jetty Alignment
project.description:
Four ways to put Stubborn's stub runner on a Spring Boot 4.1 classpath next to a spring-boot-starter-jetty application, and what each one actually does at runtime.
Jetty 12 ships as one product under several groupIds. Spring Boot 4.1 imports jetty-bom and jetty-ee11-bom, so it manages the core (org.eclipse.jetty) and the Jakarta EE 11 layer -- but NOT org.eclipse.jetty.ee10, which is the servlet layer wiremock-jetty12 is built against. Nothing in Boot's BOM has an opinion about ee10, so it resolves to whatever wiremock-jetty12 declares: 12.0.30.
An ee10 on one minor line and a core on another do not fail to resolve. They fail when the stub server starts, because jetty-ee10-servlet's own ServletContextHandler calls Environment.ensure in its static initializer and that signature changed between 12.0 and 12.1:
NoSuchMethodError: org.eclipse.jetty.util.component.Environment.ensure(String)
Each module below is one combination, and its tests assert what really happens -- including the two that are supposed to break. Read them in order:
a-no-bom core 12.1.x + ee10 12.0.30. The stub server dies. This is the bug as reported in stubborn-sh/stubborn#142. b-bom-only Stubborn's BOM and nothing else, which is what a user actually writes. What this proves depends on the Stubborn version pinned in it, and the release automation rewrites that: on 0.2.0 the BOM pins all of Jetty to 12.0.x and the application stops starting; from 0.2.1 it manages only ee10 and both halves work. One of its two test classes runs and the other is skipped, so it is green either side of the fix and starts proving it the day the bump lands. c-ee10-aligned ee10 imported at Boot's own Jetty version by hand. Everything lands on one line and both halves work. This is the fix to apply yourself on 0.2.0; from 0.2.1 Stubborn's BOM does it and the import can go. d-shaded-standalone wiremock-standalone, whose Jetty is relocated. Both halves work, but Stubborn's response-template helpers cannot be registered against it, which is why this is not the answer.
Run `./mvnw clean test` here to see all four.
